title: CEE 102 - Engineering Data, Statistics and Probability

items.q: The compressive strengths recorded are 25, 50, 74, 75, 92, 23 N/mm². Find the range.
items.s: Range = largest − smallest = 92 − 23 = 69.

items.q: A bin holds 9 sound bolts and 9 defective bolts. If one bolt is picked at random, find the probability that it is sound.
items.s: Total bolts = 9 + 9 = 18. Probability = 9 ÷ 18 = 0.5.

items.q: The values 41, 17, 62, 6, 67, 45 are obtained from a soil test. Find the median.
items.s: Arrange in order: 6, 17, 41, 45, 62, 67. With 6 values the median is the mean of the 3th and 4th values, which gives 43.

items.q: In a set of sieve analysis results the values 92, 21, 88, 21, 21, 65 are recorded. What is the modal value?
items.s: 21 appears 3 times while every other value appears once, so the mode is 21.

items.q: For the observations 46, 29, 11, 33, 33, 39 taken as a complete population, find the variance.
items.s: Mean = 191 ÷ 6 = 31.83. Sum of squared deviations = 696.83. Variance = 696.83 ÷ 6 = 116.14.

items.q: The population values 45, 41, 17, 37, 42, 58 are measured. Determine the standard deviation.
items.s: Mean = 40. Variance = 892 ÷ 6 = 148.67. Standard deviation = √148.67 = 12.19.

items.q: A sample of 6 specimens gives the values 48, 42, 44, 45, 63, 13. Estimate the sample standard deviation.
items.s: Mean = 42.5. Sum of squared deviations = 1329.5. Sample variance = 1329.5 ÷ 5 = 265.9. Standard deviation = √265.9 = 16.31.

items.q: A set of 5 diameter readings 65, 59, 47, 50, 29 has been reduced to a mean and standard deviation. Find the coefficient of variation as a percentage.
items.s: Mean = 50 and standard deviation = 12.3. Coefficient of variation = (12.3 ÷ 50) × 100 = 24.59 per cent.

items.q: Grouped data has class marks 24, 44 and 56 with frequencies 11, 7 and 11. Calculate the mean of the grouped data.
In a construction risk study P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.45 and P(A and B) = 0.12. Find P(A or B).
Two pumps fail independently, with probabilities 0.6 and 0.3. Find the probability that both fail.
items.s: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.6 × 0.3 = 0.18.

items.q: In a defect study P(A and B) = 0.15 and P(B) = 0.6. Find P(A given B).
In how many ways can 8 distinct machine parts be arranged in 3 positions of an assembly?
items.s: Number of permutations = 8! ÷ (8 − 3)! = 336.

items.q: A supervisor must choose 3 workers from a team of 8 to inspect a site. In how many ways can the choice be made?
items.s: Number of combinations = 8! ÷ (3! × 5!) = 56.

items.q: A component is defective with probability 0.3. In a batch of 6 components, find the probability that exactly 3 are defective, assuming a binomial model.
Vehicles arrive at a weighbridge at an average of 3 per minute. Using a Poisson model, find the probability of exactly 0 arrivals in one minute.
Cube strengths are normally distributed with mean 25 N/mm² and standard deviation 4 N/mm². Find the standard score of a cube measuring 33 N/mm².
For a set of paired engineering readings, Σxy − n x̄ȳ = 12, Σx² − n x̄² = 20 and Σy² − n ȳ² = 40. Find the coefficient of correlation.
A control chart for a concrete mix has a process mean of 54 and a standard deviation of 1.5. Find the upper control limit at three sigma.
items.s: Upper control limit = mean + 3σ = 54 + (3 × 1.5) = 58.5.

items.q: The readings recorded in an engineering test are 17, 8, 28, 50, 45, 44, 57. Find the arithmetic mean, correct to two decimal places.
items.s: Add the readings: 17 + 8 + 28 + 50 + 45 + 44 + 57 = 249. Divide by the number of readings: 249 ÷ 7 = 35.57.

items.q: The compressive strengths recorded are 79, 38, 70, 85, 26, 86 N/mm². Find the range.
items.s: Range = largest − smallest = 86 − 26 = 60.

items.q: A bin holds 4 sound bolts and 4 defective bolts. If one bolt is picked at random, find the probability that it is sound.
items.s: Total bolts = 4 + 4 = 8. Probability = 4 ÷ 8 = 0.5.

items.q: The values 24, 71, 30, 53, 6, 18, 54 are obtained from a soil test. Find the median.
items.s: Arrange in order: 6, 18, 24, 30, 53, 54, 71. With 7 values the median is the 4th value, which gives 30.

items.q: In a set of sieve analysis results the values 30, 73, 30, 42, 30, 90 are recorded. What is the modal value?
items.s: 30 appears 3 times while every other value appears once, so the mode is 30.

items.q: For the observations 49, 20, 19, 47, 43, 23 taken as a complete population, find the variance.

items.q: The population values 48, 24, 53, 55, 14 are measured. Determine the standard deviation.
items.s: Mean = 38.8. Variance = 1382.8 ÷ 5 = 276.56. Standard deviation = √276.56 = 16.63.

items.q: A sample of 7 specimens gives the values 70, 23, 14, 53, 46, 65, 15. Estimate the sample standard deviation.
items.s: Mean = 40.86. Sum of squared deviations = 3314.86. Sample variance = 3314.86 ÷ 6 = 552.48. Standard deviation = √552.48 = 23.5.

items.q: A set of 6 diameter readings 65, 63, 76, 21, 28, 61 has been reduced to a mean and standard deviation. Find the coefficient of variation as a percentage.

items.q: A supervisor must choose 4 workers from a team of 9 to inspect a site. In how many ways can the choice be made?

items.q: The readings recorded in an engineering test are 28, 18, 24, 24, 12, 8, 34. Find the arithmetic mean, correct to two decimal places.

items.q: The values 32, 81, 64, 59, 20, 52, 69, 37, 54 are obtained from a soil test. Find the median.

items.q: In a set of sieve analysis results the values 33, 68, 33, 33, 59, 33, 42 are recorded. What is the modal value?

items.q: Which statement correctly defines class interval?
o: the range of values covered by one class of grouped data
all the outcomes of the sample space that are not in the event
a part of a population chosen to represent it
a characteristic recorded as a measurand rather than a category
items.s: class interval: the range of values covered by one class of grouped data. The other options describe complement of an event, sample, quantitative variable.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines sample space.
o: the running total of frequencies up to a given class
the variable being predicted in a regression relationship
the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment
a numerical value determined by the outcome of an experiment
items.s: sample space: the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment. The other options describe dependent variable, cumulative frequency, random variable.

items.q: Which of the following best describes scatter diagram?
o: a set of outcomes from the sample space that concerns us
the plot of one variable against another to show their relationship
a scale with equal intervals and a true zero point
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation
items.s: scatter diagram: the plot of one variable against another to show their relationship. The other options describe range, ratio scale, event.

items.q: Which of the following best describes population?
o: a scale with equal differences but no true zero point
the whole set of items about which information is wanted
events whose occurrence does not affect one another
the collection of data from every member of a population
items.s: population: the whole set of items about which information is wanted. The other options describe census, independent events, interval scale.

items.q: Which term is described by “sampling in which the population is divided into groups and each is sampled”?
o: primary data
population
stratified sampling
class mark
items.s: stratified sampling is sampling in which the population is divided into groups and each is sampled.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines independent events.
o: events whose occurrence does not affect one another
a characteristic recorded as a category rather than a number
the probability that two events occur together
the mean computed from class marks multiplied by class frequencies
items.s: independent events: events whose occurrence does not affect one another. The other options describe joint probability, grouped mean, qualitative variable.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines binomial distribution?
o: the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment
the product of a whole number with all the whole numbers below it
a scale with equal differences but no true zero point
the distribution of the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials
items.s: binomial distribution: the distribution of the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials. The other options describe sample space, factorial, interval scale.

items.q: accuracy may be defined as
o: a value below which a stated quarter of the observations fall
the difference between the upper and lower boundaries of a class
the closeness of a reading to the true value
a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty
items.s: accuracy: the closeness of a reading to the true value. The other options describe quartile, experiment, class width.

items.q: variable may be defined as
o: the midpoint of a class interval used to represent that class
a scale with equal intervals and a true zero point
a characteristic of an observation that can take different values
the curve drawn from cumulative frequencies against class boundaries
items.s: variable: a characteristic of an observation that can take different values. The other options describe ogive, ratio scale, class mark.

items.q: Which of the following best describes exhaustive events?
o: a variable that takes only separate countable values
events that together cover every possible outcome
a summary showing how observations are spread over their possible values
the mean of a random variable weighted by the probability of each value
items.s: exhaustive events: events that together cover every possible outcome. The other options describe expected value, discrete variable, frequency distribution.

items.q: Which of the following best describes binomial distribution?
o: the closeness of repeated readings to one another
events whose occurrence does not affect one another
events that together cover every possible outcome
the distribution of the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials
items.s: binomial distribution: the distribution of the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials. The other options describe exhaustive events, independent events, precision.

items.q: Which of the following best describes joint probability?
o: the difference between a measured value and its true value
measurements and observations gathered to describe the behaviour of an engineering system
the probability that two events occur together
the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean
items.s: joint probability: the probability that two events occur together. The other options describe measurement error, coefficient of variation, engineering data.

items.q: Which of the following best describes addition rule?
o: the rule that the probability of either of two events is their sum less their overlap
a numerical value determined by the outcome of an experiment
the curve drawn from cumulative frequencies against class boundaries
the boundaries beyond which a process is judged out of control
items.s: addition rule: the rule that the probability of either of two events is their sum less their overlap. The other options describe ogive, random variable, control limits.

items.q: Which of the following best describes coefficient of variation?
o: a mean in which each value is multiplied by a weight of importance
the collection of data from every member of a population
a numerical characteristic computed from a sample
the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean
items.s: coefficient of variation: the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean. The other options describe weighted mean, census, statistic.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines event?
o: a set of outcomes from the sample space that concerns us
an arrangement of objects in which the order matters
judging a lot of items by inspecting a sample drawn from it
the positive square root of the variance
items.s: event: a set of outcomes from the sample space that concerns us. The other options describe acceptance sampling, standard deviation, permutation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes acceptance sampling?
o: the true upper or lower limit between adjoining class intervals
a probability distribution whose variable takes separate values
judging a lot of items by inspecting a sample drawn from it
the measure of how likely an event is, from zero to one
items.s: acceptance sampling: judging a lot of items by inspecting a sample drawn from it. The other options describe discrete distribution, probability, class boundary.

items.q: Which of the following best describes open ended class?
o: all the outcomes of the sample space that are not in the event
a class interval with no stated upper or lower limit
the line on a control chart that marks the process average
data that already exist and were gathered for another purpose
items.s: open ended class: a class interval with no stated upper or lower limit. The other options describe central line, secondary data, complement of an event.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines range.
o: error that varies unsystematically from one reading to another
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation
an arrangement of objects in which the order matters
the closeness of a reading to the true value
items.s: range: the difference between the largest and the smallest observation. The other options describe permutation, accuracy, random error.

items.q: The statement “the line on a control chart that marks the process average” describes which of the following?
o: quality control chart
control limits
assignable cause
central line
items.s: central line is the line on a control chart that marks the process average.

items.q: Which of the following best describes tally?
o: a mark kept to count occurrences while recording data
a characteristic recorded as a category rather than a number
an arrangement of objects in which the order matters
a numerical characteristic computed from a sample
items.s: tally: a mark kept to count occurrences while recording data. The other options describe permutation, statistic, qualitative variable.

items.q: permutation may be defined as
o: an arrangement of objects in which the order matters
a smooth curve drawn through plotted points to show the general behaviour of data
a variable that takes only separate countable values
the sum of the values divided by the number of values
items.s: permutation: an arrangement of objects in which the order matters. The other options describe freehand curve, arithmetic mean, discrete variable.

items.q: All of the following belong to Probability axioms EXCEPT
o: event
sample space
experiment
arithmetic mean
items.s: Every other option belongs to Probability axioms. “arithmetic mean” belongs to Central tendency, not Probability axioms.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines sample space?
o: error that shifts every reading in the same direction
the line on a control chart that marks the process average
the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment
the probability that two events occur together
items.s: sample space: the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment. The other options describe joint probability, central line, systematic error.

items.q: Which of the following best describes class width?
o: the mean of a random variable weighted by the probability of each value
the difference between the upper and lower boundaries of a class
choosing a sample so that every member has an equal chance of selection
the range of values covered by one class of grouped data
items.s: class width: the difference between the upper and lower boundaries of a class. The other options describe expected value, class interval, random sampling.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines regression line?
o: the average of the absolute departures of observations from the mean
all the outcomes of the sample space that are not in the event
the line that best fits the plotted points for predicting one variable from another
data that already exist and were gathered for another purpose
items.s: regression line: the line that best fits the plotted points for predicting one variable from another. The other options describe mean deviation, secondary data, complement of an event.

items.q: The statement “events that together cover every possible outcome” describes which of the following?
o: exhaustive events
experiment
probability
complement of an event
items.s: exhaustive events is events that together cover every possible outcome.

items.q: The statement “the average squared departure of the observations from their mean” describes which of the following?
o: coefficient of variation
variance
statistic
parameter
items.s: variance is the average squared departure of the observations from their mean.

items.q: Which of the following best describes discrete distribution?
o: a scale in which values are simply names with no order
events whose occurrence does not affect one another
choosing a sample so that every member has an equal chance of selection
a probability distribution whose variable takes separate values
items.s: discrete distribution: a probability distribution whose variable takes separate values. The other options describe random sampling, nominal scale, independent events.

items.q: systematic error may be defined as
o: a numerical characteristic computed from a sample
a smooth curve drawn through plotted points to show the general behaviour of data
error that shifts every reading in the same direction
the closeness of a reading to the true value
items.s: systematic error: error that shifts every reading in the same direction. The other options describe freehand curve, accuracy, statistic.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines random error.
o: error that varies unsystematically from one reading to another
a summary showing how observations are spread over their possible values
sampling in which the population is divided into groups and each is sampled
a scale in which the values may be ranked but the gaps are unequal
items.s: random error: error that varies unsystematically from one reading to another. The other options describe stratified sampling, frequency distribution, ordinal scale.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines ordinal scale.
o: a mark kept to count occurrences while recording data
the mean computed from class marks multiplied by class frequencies
a scale in which the values may be ranked but the gaps are unequal
a mean in which each value is multiplied by a weight of importance
items.s: ordinal scale: a scale in which the values may be ranked but the gaps are unequal. The other options describe tally, weighted mean, grouped mean.

items.q: Which term is described by “a set of outcomes from the sample space that concerns us”?
o: sample space
equally likely outcomes
event
exhaustive events
items.s: event is a set of outcomes from the sample space that concerns us.

items.q: Which of the following best describes factorial?
o: the product of a whole number with all the whole numbers below it
the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment
the closeness of a reading to the true value
a set of outcomes from the sample space that concerns us
items.s: factorial: the product of a whole number with all the whole numbers below it. The other options describe accuracy, event, sample space.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines assignable cause?
o: the difference between the largest and the smallest observation
a specific identifiable reason for a process going out of control
sampling in which the population is divided into groups and each is sampled
the average squared departure of the observations from their mean
items.s: assignable cause: a specific identifiable reason for a process going out of control. The other options describe stratified sampling, range, variance.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines interval scale?
o: an arrangement of objects in which the order matters
events that cannot both occur in the same trial
the rule that the probability of either of two events is their sum less their overlap
a scale with equal differences but no true zero point
items.s: interval scale: a scale with equal differences but no true zero point. The other options describe addition rule, permutation, mutually exclusive events.

items.q: All of the following belong to Quality control charts EXCEPT
o: quality control chart
central line
precision
control limits
items.s: Every other option belongs to Quality control charts. “precision” belongs to Engineering data and measurement scales, not Quality control charts.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines open ended class?
o: measurements and observations gathered to describe the behaviour of an engineering system
events that together cover every possible outcome
the closeness of a reading to the true value
a class interval with no stated upper or lower limit
items.s: open ended class: a class interval with no stated upper or lower limit. The other options describe accuracy, engineering data, exhaustive events.

items.q: Which term is described by “a bar chart in which the bars touch and the areas show the frequencies”?
o: cumulative frequency
class width
open ended class
histogram
items.s: histogram is a bar chart in which the bars touch and the areas show the frequencies.

items.q: Which of the following best describes class boundary?
o: a set of outcomes from the sample space that concerns us
a mean in which each value is multiplied by a weight of importance
a part of a population chosen to represent it
the true upper or lower limit between adjoining class intervals
items.s: class boundary: the true upper or lower limit between adjoining class intervals. The other options describe event, sample, weighted mean.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines grouped mean.
o: data that already exist and were gathered for another purpose
events that cannot both occur in the same trial
the mean computed from class marks multiplied by class frequencies
the list from which the members of a sample are drawn
items.s: grouped mean: the mean computed from class marks multiplied by class frequencies. The other options describe mutually exclusive events, sampling frame, secondary data.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines independent events?
o: events whose occurrence does not affect one another
a part of a population chosen to represent it
the plot of one variable against another to show their relationship
a mark kept to count occurrences while recording data
items.s: independent events: events whose occurrence does not affect one another. The other options describe scatter diagram, sample, tally.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines permutation.
o: the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment
a numerical value determined by the outcome of an experiment
error that shifts every reading in the same direction
an arrangement of objects in which the order matters
items.s: permutation: an arrangement of objects in which the order matters. The other options describe random variable, systematic error, sample space.

items.q: The statement “a variable able to take any value in a range, such as length” describes which of the following?
o: interval scale
measurement error
ordinal scale
continuous variable
items.s: continuous variable is a variable able to take any value in a range, such as length.

items.q: The statement “the product of a whole number with all the whole numbers below it” describes which of the following?
o: fundamental counting principle
factorial
combination
permutation
items.s: factorial is the product of a whole number with all the whole numbers below it.

items.q: The statement “the middle value when the observations are arranged in order of size” describes which of the following?
o: grouped mean
median
skewness
mode
items.s: median is the middle value when the observations are arranged in order of size.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines acceptance sampling.
o: a specific identifiable reason for a process going out of control
a value below which a stated quarter of the observations fall
judging a lot of items by inspecting a sample drawn from it
the collection of data from every member of a population
items.s: acceptance sampling: judging a lot of items by inspecting a sample drawn from it. The other options describe quartile, assignable cause, census.

items.q: The statement “sampling in which the population is divided into groups and each is sampled” describes which of the following?
o: census
frequency table
stratified sampling
population
items.s: stratified sampling is sampling in which the population is divided into groups and each is sampled.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines class boundary.
o: the average of the absolute departures of observations from the mean
an arrangement of objects in which the order matters
the boundaries beyond which a process is judged out of control
the true upper or lower limit between adjoining class intervals
items.s: class boundary: the true upper or lower limit between adjoining class intervals. The other options describe control limits, mean deviation, permutation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines random sampling?
o: a summary showing how observations are spread over their possible values
a variable that takes only separate countable values
choosing a sample so that every member has an equal chance of selection
a smooth curve drawn through plotted points to show the general behaviour of data
items.s: random sampling: choosing a sample so that every member has an equal chance of selection. The other options describe frequency distribution, discrete variable, freehand curve.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines standard deviation?
o: a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty
the positive square root of the variance
the distribution of the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials
the mean of a random variable weighted by the probability of each value
items.s: standard deviation: the positive square root of the variance. The other options describe binomial distribution, experiment, expected value.

items.q: Which of the following best describes skewness?
o: the middle value when the observations are arranged in order of size
the whole set of items about which information is wanted
the true upper or lower limit between adjoining class intervals
the tendency of a distribution to trail off to one side of its centre
items.s: skewness: the tendency of a distribution to trail off to one side of its centre. The other options describe median, population, class boundary.

items.q: range may be defined as
o: the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment
the difference between the largest and the smallest observation
the closeness of repeated readings to one another
a bar chart in which the bars touch and the areas show the frequencies
items.s: range: the difference between the largest and the smallest observation. The other options describe precision, sample space, histogram.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines median?

o: error that varies unsystematically from one reading to another
a scale with equal differences but no true zero point
error that shifts every reading in the same direction
the closeness of a reading to the true value
items.s: systematic error: error that shifts every reading in the same direction. The other options describe accuracy, random error, interval scale.

items.q: In this course, arithmetic mean refers to
o: the middle value when the observations are arranged in order of size
the mean computed from class marks multiplied by class frequencies
a mean in which each value is multiplied by a weight of importance
the sum of the values divided by the number of values
items.s: arithmetic mean: the sum of the values divided by the number of values. The other options describe weighted mean, median, grouped mean.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains random variable.
o: the mean of a random variable weighted by the probability of each value
the distribution of the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials
a probability distribution whose variable takes separate values
a numerical value determined by the outcome of an experiment
items.s: random variable: a numerical value determined by the outcome of an experiment. The other options describe binomial distribution, discrete distribution, expected value.

items.q: In this course, class width refers to
o: a bar chart in which the bars touch and the areas show the frequencies
the difference between the upper and lower boundaries of a class
a class interval with no stated upper or lower limit
the running total of frequencies up to a given class
items.s: class width: the difference between the upper and lower boundaries of a class. The other options describe cumulative frequency, open ended class, histogram.

items.q: The correct meaning of median is
o: the middle value when the observations are arranged in order of size
a mean in which each value is multiplied by a weight of importance
the tendency of a distribution to trail off to one side of its centre
the mean computed from class marks multiplied by class frequencies
items.s: median: the middle value when the observations are arranged in order of size. The other options describe weighted mean, skewness, grouped mean.

items.q: “a scale in which values are simply names with no order” is the definition of
o: qualitative variable
engineering data
interval scale
nominal scale
items.s: nominal scale is a scale in which values are simply names with no order.

items.q: In this course, central line refers to
o: a specific identifiable reason for a process going out of control
judging a lot of items by inspecting a sample drawn from it
the line on a control chart that marks the process average
the boundaries beyond which a process is judged out of control
items.s: central line: the line on a control chart that marks the process average. The other options describe acceptance sampling, control limits, assignable cause.

items.q: The correct meaning of frequency table is
o: the collection of data from every member of a population
the midpoint of a class interval used to represent that class
a table showing how often each value or class occurs
a mark kept to count occurrences while recording data
items.s: frequency table: a table showing how often each value or class occurs. The other options describe class mark, tally, census.

items.q: “the closeness of repeated readings to one another” is the definition of
o: measurement error
engineering data
precision
variable
items.s: precision is the closeness of repeated readings to one another.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a numerical characteristic computed from a sample”
o: variance
quartile
range
statistic
items.s: statistic is a numerical characteristic computed from a sample.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines scatter diagram?
o: the variable being predicted in a regression relationship
the measure of the strength and direction of a linear relationship, from minus one to one
the plot of one variable against another to show their relationship
the line that best fits the plotted points for predicting one variable from another
items.s: scatter diagram: the plot of one variable against another to show their relationship. The other options describe dependent variable, regression line, correlation coefficient.

items.q: “the midpoint of a class interval used to represent that class” is the definition of
o: random sampling
population
class mark
primary data
items.s: class mark is the midpoint of a class interval used to represent that class.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains discrete variable.
o: a characteristic recorded as a category rather than a number
a variable that takes only separate countable values
measurements and observations gathered to describe the behaviour of an engineering system
a characteristic recorded as a measurand rather than a category
items.s: discrete variable: a variable that takes only separate countable values. The other options describe quantitative variable, engineering data, qualitative variable.

items.q: In this course, experiment refers to
o: outcomes no one of which is more probable than the others
all the outcomes of the sample space that are not in the event
the measure of how likely an event is, from zero to one
a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty
items.s: experiment: a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty. The other options describe complement of an event, probability, equally likely outcomes.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains ordinal scale.
o: a scale in which the values may be ranked but the gaps are unequal
the closeness of repeated readings to one another
a characteristic of an observation that can take different values
measurements and observations gathered to describe the behaviour of an engineering system
items.s: ordinal scale: a scale in which the values may be ranked but the gaps are unequal. The other options describe engineering data, variable, precision.

items.q: The correct meaning of class boundary is
o: the true upper or lower limit between adjoining class intervals
the difference between the upper and lower boundaries of a class
the curve drawn from cumulative frequencies against class boundaries
the range of values covered by one class of grouped data
items.s: class boundary: the true upper or lower limit between adjoining class intervals. The other options describe ogive, class width, class interval.

items.q: “the difference between the upper and lower boundaries of a class” is the definition of
o: class interval
class width
freehand curve
open ended class
items.s: class width is the difference between the upper and lower boundaries of a class.

items.q: “outcomes no one of which is more probable than the others” is the definition of
o: probability
equally likely outcomes
sample space
experiment
items.s: equally likely outcomes is outcomes no one of which is more probable than the others.

items.q: The correct meaning of binomial distribution is
o: the mean of a random variable weighted by the probability of each value
the distribution of the count of rare events in a fixed interval
the distribution of the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials
a numerical value determined by the outcome of an experiment
items.s: binomial distribution: the distribution of the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials. The other options describe random variable, expected value, poisson distribution.

items.q: “error that varies unsystematically from one reading to another” is the definition of
o: random error
ratio scale
engineering data
interval scale
items.s: random error is error that varies unsystematically from one reading to another.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains regression line.
o: the line that best fits the plotted points for predicting one variable from another
the plot of one variable against another to show their relationship
the variable being predicted in a regression relationship
the measure of the strength and direction of a linear relationship, from minus one to one
items.s: regression line: the line that best fits the plotted points for predicting one variable from another. The other options describe scatter diagram, correlation coefficient, dependent variable.

items.q: “a part of a population chosen to represent it” is the definition of
o: sample
secondary data
stratified sampling
population
items.s: sample is a part of a population chosen to represent it.

items.q: In this course, secondary data refers to
o: a part of a population chosen to represent it
the collection of data from every member of a population
data that already exist and were gathered for another purpose
a mark kept to count occurrences while recording data
items.s: secondary data: data that already exist and were gathered for another purpose. The other options describe sample, census, tally.

items.q: “the probability that two events occur together” is the definition of
o: independent events
joint probability
multiplication rule
addition rule
items.s: joint probability is the probability that two events occur together.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the whole set of items about which information is wanted”
o: population
sampling frame
tally
stratified sampling
items.s: population is the whole set of items about which information is wanted.

items.q: In this course, primary data refers to
o: sampling in which the population is divided into groups and each is sampled
a mark kept to count occurrences while recording data
data collected first hand by the investigator for the present purpose
a part of a population chosen to represent it
items.s: primary data: data collected first hand by the investigator for the present purpose. The other options describe sample, stratified sampling, tally.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains mode.
o: the tendency of a distribution to trail off to one side of its centre
a mean in which each value is multiplied by a weight of importance
the value that occurs with the greatest frequency
the middle value when the observations are arranged in order of size
items.s: mode: the value that occurs with the greatest frequency. The other options describe weighted mean, skewness, median.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains continuous variable.
o: a variable able to take any value in a range, such as length
a scale in which the values may be ranked but the gaps are unequal
a characteristic recorded as a measurand rather than a category
a scale with equal differences but no true zero point
items.s: continuous variable: a variable able to take any value in a range, such as length. The other options describe quantitative variable, ordinal scale, interval scale.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “data that already exist and were gathered for another purpose”
o: primary data
sample
random sampling
secondary data
items.s: secondary data is data that already exist and were gathered for another purpose.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the middle value when the observations are arranged in order of size”
o: skewness
median
arithmetic mean
mode
items.s: median is the middle value when the observations are arranged in order of size.

items.q: “a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty” is the definition of
o: experiment
mutually exclusive events
equally likely outcomes
probability
items.s: experiment is a procedure whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty.

items.q: coefficient of variation may be defined as
o: the difference between the largest and the smallest observation
the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean
a numerical characteristic of a whole population
the average squared departure of the observations from their mean
items.s: coefficient of variation: the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean. The other options describe parameter, range, variance.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a scale with equal intervals and a true zero point”
o: ratio scale
quantitative variable
engineering data
systematic error
items.s: ratio scale is a scale with equal intervals and a true zero point.

items.q: “the tendency of a distribution to trail off to one side of its centre” is the definition of
o: median
skewness
grouped mean
arithmetic mean
items.s: skewness is the tendency of a distribution to trail off to one side of its centre.

items.q: The correct meaning of mutually exclusive events is
o: a set of outcomes from the sample space that concerns us
all the outcomes of the sample space that are not in the event
outcomes no one of which is more probable than the others
events that cannot both occur in the same trial
items.s: mutually exclusive events: events that cannot both occur in the same trial. The other options describe equally likely outcomes, event, complement of an event.

items.q: The correct meaning of grouped mean is
o: the sum of the values divided by the number of values
the mean computed from class marks multiplied by class frequencies
the middle value when the observations are arranged in order of size
the tendency of a distribution to trail off to one side of its centre
items.s: grouped mean: the mean computed from class marks multiplied by class frequencies. The other options describe median, skewness, arithmetic mean.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “outcomes no one of which is more probable than the others”
o: event
experiment
sample space
equally likely outcomes
items.s: equally likely outcomes is outcomes no one of which is more probable than the others.

items.q: In this course, class mark refers to
o: data collected first hand by the investigator for the present purpose
a part of a population chosen to represent it
the whole set of items about which information is wanted
the midpoint of a class interval used to represent that class
items.s: class mark: the midpoint of a class interval used to represent that class. The other options describe primary data, sample, population.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the plot of one variable against another to show their relationship”
o: correlation coefficient
regression line
scatter diagram
dependent variable
items.s: scatter diagram is the plot of one variable against another to show their relationship.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines factorial?
o: a selection of objects in which the order does not matter
the product of a whole number with all the whole numbers below it
an arrangement of objects in which the order matters
the rule that independent choices multiply to give the number of outcomes
items.s: factorial: the product of a whole number with all the whole numbers below it. The other options describe fundamental counting principle, permutation, combination.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the average squared departure of the observations from their mean”
o: range
mean deviation
variance
parameter
items.s: variance is the average squared departure of the observations from their mean.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains coefficient of variation.
o: the average squared departure of the observations from their mean
the positive square root of the variance
a numerical characteristic of a whole population
the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean
items.s: coefficient of variation: the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean. The other options describe parameter, variance, standard deviation.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains qualitative variable.
o: a characteristic recorded as a category rather than a number
a scale in which the values may be ranked but the gaps are unequal
measurements and observations gathered to describe the behaviour of an engineering system
the closeness of a reading to the true value
items.s: qualitative variable: a characteristic recorded as a category rather than a number. The other options describe ordinal scale, engineering data, accuracy.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains event.
o: all the outcomes of the sample space that are not in the event
a set of outcomes from the sample space that concerns us
outcomes no one of which is more probable than the others
events that cannot both occur in the same trial
items.s: event: a set of outcomes from the sample space that concerns us. The other options describe mutually exclusive events, equally likely outcomes, complement of an event.

items.q: “the positive square root of the variance” is the definition of
o: parameter
mean deviation
quartile
standard deviation
items.s: standard deviation is the positive square root of the variance.

items.q: In this course, accuracy refers to
o: a scale in which the values may be ranked but the gaps are unequal
the closeness of a reading to the true value
a characteristic recorded as a category rather than a number
a scale in which values are simply names with no order
items.s: accuracy: the closeness of a reading to the true value. The other options describe qualitative variable, ordinal scale, nominal scale.

items.q: “data collected first hand by the investigator for the present purpose” is the definition of
o: primary data
class mark
secondary data
sample
items.s: primary data is data collected first hand by the investigator for the present purpose.
